notes: Everything quantum is simulated on a classical computer (statevector Grover Adaptive Search, path-integral Monte Carlo SQA); no quantum speed-up is claimed.
Stage 2 shows no SQA advantage over classical SA: the classical control was better on medium and large at both budgets, every seed (Step 2D.4).
Stage 1 on small_v2: 351 GAS oracle calls + measurements vs 256 exhaustive evaluations. At m = 8 (small, medium) GAS costs more than exhaustive (R7); on large it is 1,053 vs 4,096.
The constraint-preserving SQA (one-hot hopping driver) is not runnable on today's quantum annealers, which only offer a transverse-field driver.
Quantization loss on small_v2: the best placement of the quantized model (unit 0.0025 NCU) costs +0.000 % joules vs the real-size exact optimum R1, so a quantized optimum can still lose to R1.
caveats: Validity of a method is valid_real: the placement fits the real server capacities (shared validator).

valid_quantized only says whether the placement also fits the quantum model's rounding grid (unit 0.0025 NCU); the baselines and R1 work at real sizes, so a failed quantized check is expected for them and is not an error.
The baselines' CloudSim host model rounds CPU to that grid and keeps memory at its real size, the generous choice for the baselines.

Methods are ranked by linear joules (diff_r1_pct), the optimised objective. it_energy_kwh comes from the SPEC power curve, on which the quantum placement can score below R1 (small, medium) although R1 is optimal for the linear objective; this is not a win over the optimum.

The cached quantum and control rows come from one Stage-2 seed (pipe_stage2_seed 0). The multi-seed comparison (Step 2D.4: held-out seeds 0-2, budgets B and 4B, medium and large) found classical SA better than SQA in 4 of 4 cells, for every seed.
A live run uses the same config seeds as the cached result, so it must reproduce it; matches_cached reports this.

methods.label: Quantum pipeline (GAS -> constraint-preserving SQA)
methods.algorithm: Grover Adaptive Search (statevector simulation) picks the servers to switch on; constraint-preserving simulated quantum annealing (path-integral Monte Carlo) places the VMs on them.
methods.reference: Dürr & Høyer 1996, arXiv:quant-ph/9607014 (quantum minimum finding); Gilliam, Woerner & Gonciulea 2021, Quantum 5, 428 (Grover Adaptive Search); Hen & Spedalieri 2016, Phys. Rev. Applied 5, 034007 and Hen & Sarandy 2016, Phys. Rev. A 93, 062312 (constraint-preserving drivers); Martoňák, Santoro & Tosatti 2002, Phys. Rev. B 66, 094203 (path-integral SQA)

methods.label: Classical control (GAS -> constraint-preserving SA)
methods.algorithm: Same Stage 1 and the same moves and budget as the quantum pipeline, with classical simulated annealing in Stage 2.

methods.label: Exact optimum R1 (MILP, real sizes)
methods.algorithm: Mixed-integer linear program on the real VM sizes (SciPy HiGHS), proven optimal for the linear energy model; the reference every method is compared with.
methods.reference: Huangfu & Hall 2018, Math. Prog. Comp. 10, 119 (HiGHS); Virtanen et al. 2020, Nature Methods 17, 261 (SciPy milp)

methods.label: CloudSim FirstFit (next-fit)
methods.algorithm: CloudSim Plus 8.0.0 built-in VmAllocationPolicyFirstFit, VMs in input order; it resumes at the last used host, so it behaves as circular next-fit.
methods.reference: CloudSim Plus 8.0.0, VmAllocationPolicyFirstFit; Silva Filho et al. 2017, IFIP/IEEE IM (CloudSim Plus)

methods.label: CloudSim BestFit
methods.algorithm: CloudSim Plus 8.0.0 built-in VmAllocationPolicyBestFit (active host with the fewest free CPU units), VMs in input order.
methods.reference: CloudSim Plus 8.0.0, VmAllocationPolicyBestFit; Silva Filho et al. 2017, IFIP/IEEE IM (CloudSim Plus)

methods.label: CloudSim WorstFit (Simple)
methods.algorithm: CloudSim Plus 8.0.0 built-in VmAllocationPolicySimple (active host with the most free CPU units), VMs in input order.
methods.reference: CloudSim Plus 8.0.0, VmAllocationPolicySimple; Silva Filho et al. 2017, IFIP/IEEE IM (CloudSim Plus)

methods.label: CloudSim RoundRobin
methods.algorithm: CloudSim Plus 8.0.0 built-in VmAllocationPolicyRoundRobin, VMs in input order.
methods.reference: CloudSim Plus 8.0.0, VmAllocationPolicyRoundRobin; Silva Filho et al. 2017, IFIP/IEEE IM (CloudSim Plus)

methods.label: First-Fit Decreasing
methods.algorithm: Textbook first-fit (lowest-index host that fits) with VMs sorted by CPU size descending, run in CloudSim Plus.

methods.label: Best-Fit Decreasing
methods.algorithm: CloudSim Plus 8.0.0 built-in VmAllocationPolicyBestFit with VMs sorted by CPU size descending.

methods.label: PABFD (implemented per Beloglazov & Buyya 2012)
methods.algorithm: Power-Aware Best-Fit Decreasing: VMs by CPU descending, each to the host with the smallest power increase (SPEC curve; an empty host is off). Not built into CloudSim Plus 8; implemented on its allocation hook.
methods.reference: Beloglazov & Buyya 2012, Concurrency Computat.: Pract. Exper. 24(13), 1397 (PABFD)
